extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, volunteer reviewers, Scientific Review Officers (SROs), and NIH Institute/Center staff involved in NIH peer review of research grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH guidance describing the roles, procedures, scored review criteria, additional considerations, scoring rules, appeals, second-level review, and post-review steps for peer review of NIH research grant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should be fair, equitable, timely, and free of bias; these core values form the foundation for the laws, regulations, and policies that govern NIH peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH's dual peer review system is mandated by statute (Public Health Service Act §492) and federal regulations. Processes should promote evaluation based on these core values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA-specified review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) specifies all review criteria and considerations that will be used to evaluate applications submitted for that FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RFAs and certain Program Announcements may include additional review criteria. Unless the FOA specifies otherwise, standard NIH review procedures apply (including NOT-OD-09-024 scoring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRO is the federal official responsible for ensuring each application receives an objective and fair initial peer review and that applicable laws, regulations, and policies are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs analyze application content and completeness; document and manage conflicts of interest; recruit qualified reviewers; assign applications to reviewers; oversee administrative and regulatory aspects of meetings; and prepare summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should be recruited based on scientific and technical qualifications and other considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific desirable attributes include: authority in their scientific field, dedication to high-quality fair and objective reviews, ability to work collegially in a group, experience in research grant review, and balanced representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare conflicts of interest with specific applications following NIH guidance and SROs must document and manage conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicted reviewers do not participate in scoring/discussion for those applications; see Managing Conflict of Interest in NIH Peer Review guidance for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and integrity of the peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and applicants must maintain confidentiality of peer review information; applicants must not contact reviewers or attempt to influence outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who contact reviewers, send information directly to reviewers, or access review-related information may face consequences. See Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities: timing and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned reviewers receive access to applications about six weeks prior to the meeting and must prepare written critiques and assign numerical criterion scores as directed by the SRO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers submit critiques based on review criteria, assign numerical scores for each scored criterion, make recommendations concerning scientific/technical merit, protections for human subjects, inclusion policies, vertebrate animals, biohazards, and appropriateness of budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an overall impact score reflecting their assessment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall impact score is given in consideration of the scored review criteria and applicable additional review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five scored review criteria used to evaluate research grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assign a numerical score for this criterion and consider it when determining the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the investigators' qualifications and suitability for the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a scored criterion; reviewers provide a numerical score and factor it into the overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of novelty and innovativeness of the concepts, approaches, or methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is scored and contributes to the overall impact evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses proposed to accomplish the aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This scored criterion is heavily weighted in determining overall impact and is separately scored by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the institutional support, resources, and collaborative environment available to the investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This scored criterion is considered in the overall impact determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Timeline (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications involving clinical trials, reviewers will evaluate the study timeline while determining scientific and technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This item is considered as applicable but is not given a separate numerical score and should not be counted separately in the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate protections for human subjects where applicable in determining scientific and technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed as applicable; not given a separate numerical score but factored into overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate inclusion plans for women, minorities, and children where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered as applicable; not separately scored but informs the overall impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the welfare and appropriateness of proposed vertebrate animal use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed as applicable; not given a separate score but influences overall impact and may trigger NRFC if serious ethical problems exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consider biohazard risks associated with the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated as applicable and considered in the overall impact; serious biohazard issues can lead to NRFC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, reviewers evaluate resubmitted applications in light of previous reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered in assessing merit; not separately scored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For renewal (competing continuation) applications, reviewers evaluate progress and plans for continued work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered as part of the merit assessment; not separately scored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For revisions (competing supplement) reviewers evaluate the changes proposed relative to prior submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered as applicable; not separately scored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations (additional consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consider issues specific to applications from foreign organizations when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a consideration only; reviewers should not give it a separate numerical score or include it in the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent considerations (additional consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence/use of select agents is evaluated as an additional consideration where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered but not separately scored; serious issues may affect fundability or lead to NRFC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (additional consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consider resource sharing (data, model organisms, etc.) plans as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered in review but not given a separate numerical score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources (additional consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate plans to authenticate key biological/chemical resources as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment is a consideration, not a separately scored criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period Support (additional consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consider the appropriateness of budget requests and period of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget is considered but should not be factored into the overall impact score; reviewers may comment on budget appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH scoring system and score calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) for individual criterion and overall impact scores; final overall impact scores are the mean of eligible members' final impact scores multiplied by 10 (reported as 10–90).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before meetings reviewers give preliminary criterion and overall impact scores; for discussed applications, each eligible committee member gives a final impact score. Applications not discussed are designated ND (no numerical impact score reported) and typically rank in the bottom half.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NRFC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An SRG may designate an application NRFC if it lacks significant and substantial merit or presents serious ethical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious ethical problems include inadequate protection of human subjects, misuse of vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents. NRFC applications do not proceed to second-level review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary statement content and ND reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants receive a summary statement containing reviewer written comments and scores for each scored review criterion; applications not discussed are designated ND (may be reported as ++).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary statements identify the base used to determine percentiles; applicants can use summary statements to plan resubmissions or contact the Program Official for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: A percentile approximates the percentage of applications that received a better overall impact score from the study section during the past year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentiles are reported as whole numbers; for ad hoc study sections a different base may be used; only a subset of application types are percentiled; the summary statement will identify the base used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals eligibility and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators may appeal initial peer review results if they believe the review process was flawed by reviewer bias, conflict of interest, absence of appropriate expertise, or factual errors that could have substantially altered the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appeal system (NOT-OD-11-064) does not apply to certain contract technical evaluations, NIH funding decisions, or MERIT award extension decisions. Appeals must demonstrate procedural flaws or errors, not disagreement with scientific judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level (Advisory Council/Board) review considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Councils/Boards consider program staff analyses, overall impact scores, percentile rankings (if applicable), summary statements, and the Institute/Center's goals and needs when advising on funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff provide a grant-funding plan to Council. Council members have access to applications and summary statements pending funding rounds; Council advice informs but does not replace IC director decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Council Review for large awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Council conducts a Special Council Review of applications from investigators who currently receive $1 million or more in direct NIH funding for Research Project Grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This review determines if additional funds should be provided to already well-supported investigators and does not represent a cap on NIH funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final funding decision and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Only applications recommended by both the SRG and the Advisory Council may be recommended for funding; the Institute/Center director makes final funding decisions based on staff and Council advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff examine peer review results in light of IC priorities and prepare funding plans for Council consideration; program officials and grants management officers handle subsequent award and administrative matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review applicant options and next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is not funded, applicants may resubmit addressing reviewer concerns or submit a new application; applicants are directed to 'Next Steps' guidance and may contact their Program Official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications with fundable scores, applicants should review IC paylines and funding strategies; program officials can provide guidance about likelihood of funding and next actions if application is selected for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paylines and fundable score interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ICs publish paylines to guide applicants on funding likelihood; paylines and funding strategies vary by IC and fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application scores are compared against the payline for the fiscal year when the application will be considered, which may differ from the submission year; delays may occur in announcing paylines at the beginning of fiscal years.
